newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon gets weapons destruction contract.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon gets weapons destruction contract.

text.p: Raytheon Co unit Raytheon Engineers & Constructors said Wednesday it received a $567 million contract from the U.S. Army to construct and operate a chemical weapons destruction facility in Umatilla, Ore.
The facility will be built at the Umatilla Army Depot in northeastern Oregon.

Under the contract, Raytheon said, it will perform management of the project, as well as construction, equipment procurement, start-up, operations and maintenance, and ultimately closure of the facility.

Raytheon Demilitarization Company, a unit of Raytheon Engineers, will perform the work and use Raytheon Constructors Inc for the facility construction. Project duration is nine years, the company said.
The Umatilla Army Depot stores 11.6 percent of the about 25,000 tons of chemical weapons in the U.S. stockpile.
Raytheon Engineers & Constructors is one of the four business segments of Raytheon Co.
